title: Password Reset Flow
purpose: Forgot password → resetPasswordForEmail → Supabase email → redirect → new password form → admin.updateUserById. Highlight the email-enumeration prevention (always returns success) and the fact that existing sessions are not invalidated.
description: Complete password reset flow covering two phases: (1) Forgot-password request: frontend submits email → auth service calls supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail(email) → Supabase Auth sends password reset email via SMTP with redirect link → auth service always returns success { message: 'If account exists, reset email sent' } regardless of whether the email exists (prevents email enumeration). (2) Password reset: user clicks link in email → redirected to frontend reset page with access token in URL → user submits new password → auth service calls supabase.admin.updateUserById(userId, { password }) to update via Supabase Auth admin API → password reset confirmed. Key security observations: email-enumeration prevention (always returns success regardless of email existence), existing sessions are NOT invalidated after password change (other logged-in devices remain active), requires SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY for admin API password update, and no rate limiting on the forgot-password endpoint.

validationRules: Email must be a valid format (validated by Supabase Auth API)
New password must meet Supabase Auth strength requirements
Access token from email must be valid and not expired
businessRules: Always return success for forgot-password regardless of email existence (enumeration prevention)
Reset link contains access token in URL—sent via Supabase Auth email infrastructure
Existing sessions are NOT invalidated after password change
securityConsiderations: Email-enumeration prevention: same response for existing and non-existing email
Existing sessions remain valid after password change—no forced logout
Requires SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY for admin.updateUserById (exposed in frontend .env)
Reset link token sent via URL (may be logged by email proxy or browser)
No rate limiting on forgot-password endpoint—potential for SMTP spam
performanceConsiderations: Forgot-password: single Supabase Auth API call (~100-300ms)
Reset-password: single Supabase Auth admin API call (~100-300ms)
Email delivery latency depends on Supabase Auth email infrastructure

annotations.text: Good practice: always returns success to prevent email enumeration
SECURITY ISSUE: Active sessions on other devices remain valid. User must manually log out elsewhere.
Requires SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY for admin updateUserById—same key exposed in frontend .env
Reset email sent via Supabase Auth infrastructure, NOT the application's Nodemailer (which is unused)
